Shed Book · the mockup beside the build

Seven screens, rendered from mockups/indelible.html and from the app, at the same size. Quick entry is rebuilt; the other five are not started.

The app images come from the real widget tree with seeded records, so they are what the phone draws — not a drawing of it. One pattern runs through all seven, and it is set out at the bottom.

Updated after ruling P16: the keypad is no longer on frame 1. Three taps now buy a committed lambing with a lamb on it.

3A

Quick entry — the pageRebuilt

Rebuilt. Frame 1 is the page: the event line, the live row, INDEX and the slab, with the keypad a tap away.

The ruling
Decision #21 required “a fully interactive keypad” on frame 1 and outranks the design doc, so the sheet shipped permanently open. That clause is now struck (P16) — #21's real subject, the bootstrap, is untouched.
What the arithmetic was
Never the keypad — the strips. §8 puts the six recents inside the sheet; they were built as two permanent 96 pt bands on the page. Moved, the page's fixed chrome is 388 pt and the sheet's 528, and both fit a 667 pt phone.
Now built
The live row with the tag at 44 px, the five event words on one ruled line, the + LAMB slab (its handler was () {}), and the header's date.
The budget improved
A listed animal to a committed lambing with a lamb on it is now 3 taps — §8's own claim, measured. The typed path is 6, the documented ceiling, and all six land here: the old six needed a second screen for the stroke.
3B†

Quick entry — the tag sheetRebuilt

Rebuilt. Heading, typed digits, the match list, the create line and bordered keys.

The keys
123 × 84 filled slabs sharing edges, 2 px bordered, with a 40 ms press fill. They were bare digits on 16 pt gaps with no key drawn at all — the gaps were the “empty spaces”.
The match list
Ruled rows with summaries: In pen 4 · 2h, penned animals first. Pressing one is the whole selection and costs one tap, which is the common case the app did not have.
The confirm bar you asked about
Gone. It was a bar reading Use 412 / Create 412 with no list above it to give it meaning — which is exactly why the question “what is that?” came up. The create line now sits under the matches, always present, even when there are matches.
Still off
CLOSE is centred at the top rather than a bordered box top-right, and a typed match carries no summary — the tag index holds no history, and inventing one would be the app originating a fact.
4†

Lambing entry

Not started. Right cells, none of the page around them, and the ease control is a different control.

Lambing ease
Mockup: five 64 × 64 bordered digit buttons, 1 2 3 4 5, sitting in the thumb band. Ours: four full-width sentences stacked down the page. This is the one place the docs keep a chooser, and it is specified as digits.
The live row
412 at 44 px with its tally strokes and ROW OPEN, fixed above the band so you cannot lose track of whose row is open. Absent.
The slab
+ LAMB is a 160 × 140 filled slab in the bottom-right corner — the one target you hit without looking. Ours is the words + lamb inline in a row.
Word buttons
EDIT TIME and CHANGE beside the cells they act on, and the line DERIVED FROM 3 STROKES under the birth type. None present.
1†

Flock

Not started. The rows carry a tag and nothing else — the summary is the screen.

Tag alignment
The design right-aligns tags in a fixed three-character column so 12, 77 and 91 sit under the units of 412. Ours are left-aligned, which is the exact thing the docs argue against by name.
The summary line
3 seasons · avg 2.0 · assisted twice · prolapsed 2025 under every tag. We print no summary on any row.
Trailing status
Pen 4 · 31h, and the boxed stamps TO LAMB and BARREN. Absent.
Filters
The mockup wraps them onto ruled lines because a horizontally scrolling strip needs a swipe, and swipe is banned. Ours scrolls sideways — IN TH… is already clipped.
The band
INDEX is missing; the + EWE slab is there but sits on top of a record row.
7†

Pen board

Not started. One dense 88 px row per pen, against three loose lines per pen.

The row
Mockup: pen number at 44 px, tag, lamb tally, hours right-aligned and large, all on one line. Ours stacks number, tag and hours down three lines with a gap after each.
Over threshold
OVER boxed, a † in the margin, a doubled rule, and the hours lifting to full ink — four channels, so it survives greyscale. We render none of them.
Sorting
Sorted by hours descending, so the ewe who has been penned longest is the top row. Ours is in pen order.
Empty pens
Printed as – empty – and TURNED OUT 04:12, because the board is the whole shed. We omit them.
Header and band
THE PENS · 04:12 · 2 OVER †, and the MOVE slab. Neither exists.
8

Treatments

Closest of the seven, and untouched. The safety-critical parts are all there.

What is right
The countdown, the day tally, CLEARS 3 Sept 2026 and the bordered word buttons are all built and all correct. This screen shows the components exist — they were just never used elsewhere.
Missing
The sentence DAYS NOT COPIED — READ THE BOTTLE beside REPEAT LAST. It is the one thing standing between a copied treatment and a wrong withdrawal, and it is specified verbatim.
Also missing
LAST DAY on the doubled rule, the + DOSE slab, and the MEDICINE BOOK · 2026 / ACTIVE WITHDRAWALS · 2 headers.
12

Settings

Untouched, but the word buttons now hug their label everywhere — that fix was at the component.

Empty sections
Terminology, Reminders and Season are printed as headings with no rows. The mockup fills Terminology with real editable values — ewe, gimmer, shearling, theave, hogget.
Row form
Label above, value on a rule, rule below — the same 64 px row as everywhere else. Ours are underlined words with large gaps between them.

What is actually wrong

It is one omission, seven times over: the page was never built. Every screen renders correct data using default layout — a column of text with gaps.

Fixed at the component
Word buttons hug their label. ShedTapTarget wraps its child in Center, and Center takes the maximum width offered — so every word button in the app was a full-width row with a rule running the whole way across. That is the “small word with one line behind it”, and fixing it once fixed Settings, the lamb card and the flock filters at the same time.
The spine
A 2 px madder rule at x=68, continuous down every screen, never broken by a header or a sheet. It exists on Quick entry only. Six screens have none.
The margin cell
0–68 px: the auto-captured time, the short stamp (AUTO / EDITED / STRUCK), the dagger. Built once, in the record column I added today. Nowhere else.
Ruled rows
64 px and 88 px rows sharing edges — a 2 px bottom rule and no gap. Every screen we built uses loose vertical spacing instead, which is most of why they read as sparse.
The two thumb anchors
INDEX 96 × 64 bottom-left, the corner slab 160 × 140 bottom-right. Present on one and a half screens out of seven.
The live row
The animal being written about, fixed above the band, on every screen that has a subject. Built nowhere.
Bordered controls
Word buttons, keypad keys and INDEX all carry a 2 px border in the mockup. Ours are bare text on an underline — which is exactly the “small word with one line behind it”.

One thing on this list is not a defect and should not be fixed quietly: the design's two voices — serif for the record, sans for the controls — cannot be built today. Only one typeface is bundled, and that is a recorded open ruling (decision #98 against indelible.md §3.2), not an oversight. With a single face the two voices fall back to size and weight alone, and that is a real part of why every screen reads flatter than the mockup.
